payload.headline: Tech slide continues as fear rises; trend, fear and breadth still say stand aside

summary.thesis: Both SPY and QQQ are in downtrends, below their 50- and 200-day averages. Fear is 'elevated' and rose on the day, and only 8% of stocks are above their 50-day averages. All three readings point the same way.
summary.decision: Stand aside for both long-term and swing buying, until QQQ closes above 682.54, its 200-day average and the market gate.
summary.act_at: QQQ 682.54 (market gate, above). QQQ 608.45 and SPY 689.81 (1-month lows, below).

payload.happening: On Nov 25, SPY closed at 716.7, down 0.29% on the day, 1.85% over 5 days and 7.2% over 20 days. QQQ fell more: it closed at 633.93, down 0.65% on the day, 3.88% over 5 days and 12.63% over 20 days. Both peaked for the month on Oct 28, at 772.31 for SPY and 725.61 for QQQ. Both set their 1-month lows on Nov 20, at 689.81 for SPY and 608.45 for QQQ. The past year's highest closes were 779.09 for SPY and 759.66 for QQQ, both on Oct 6. The VIX fear gauge closed at 28.29, up from 26.36. DATA reports no news since the last note.
payload.business: Trend: both indices are below their 50- and 200-day averages, which DATA classifies as a downtrend. QQQ is 7.7% below its 200-day average and 11.5% below its 50-day. SPY is 2.0% below its 200-day and 5.7% below its 50-day. So tech is weaker than the broad market. Breadth: only 8% of stocks are above their 50-day averages, which means the selling is broad and not limited to a few large names. Taken together, the readings agree: prices are falling, fear is near the top of its yearly range, and few stocks are holding up. Both indices still sit above their Nov 20 lows (QQQ 4.0% above, SPY 3.8% above), so that low is holding for now.

worth.text: This is a price-trend note, not a valuation. DATA contains no earnings or valuation inputs, so no fair-value range is given.
worth.key_assumption: No valuation is implied. The levels are price-trend markers only.

bull: Both indices are still above their Nov 20 1-month lows (QQQ 608.45, SPY 689.81), so the recent low is holding.
SPY is only 2.0% below its 200-day average of 730.77, much closer to repairing its long-term trend than QQQ.
bear: QQQ is down 12.63% over 20 days and 7.7% below its 200-day average, so the market gate at 682.54 is still far away.
Fear rose on the day, with VIX at 28.29 against 26.36 the day before. That is close to the 'high' band that starts at 30.
Breadth of 8% means almost no stocks are in short-term uptrends, so setups keep failing the pipeline's market check.

levels.what: QQQ 200-day average and the market gate. A close above it ends the tech downtrend, which would support moving to a selective stance.
QQQ 1-month low (Nov 20). A close below it would set a new 1-month low, meaning the decline would be continuing.
QQQ 50-day average. A close above it would put tech's short-term trend back up and pass the pipeline's 'QQQ above its 50-day average' check.
QQQ 1-month high (Oct 28). A close above it would mean the tech pullback is fully recovered.
SPY 1-month low (Nov 20). A close below it would set a new 1-month low, meaning the decline would be continuing.
SPY 200-day average. A close above it would put the broad market's long-term trend back up.
SPY 50-day average. A close above it would put SPY's short-term trend back up.
SPY 1-month high (Oct 28). A close above it would mean SPY's pullback is fully recovered.

longterm.why: QQQ closed at 633.93, 7.7% below its 200-day gate of 682.54. Fear is 'elevated' at 28.29 and rising, and breadth is 8%. Trend, fear and breadth all argue against new buying until QQQ closes above 682.54.

swing.why: QQQ is 11.5% below its 50-day average of 707.02. Below that level, setups keep failing the pipeline's market check, and the 0.65% drop on Nov 25 moved QQQ further away from it.

decision.timing: The next scheduled event is the jobs report (Employment Situation) on Dec 4 at 08:30, which shapes rate expectations. The nearest levels are SPY 730.77 above and 689.81 below, and QQQ 682.54 above and 608.45 below. The 50- and 200-day averages move every day, while the 1-month highs and lows are fixed past prices.

change_mind: A QQQ close above 682.54 (its 200-day average and the market gate) would end the tech downtrend and support moving from stand aside to selective. A QQQ close above 707.02 would also put tech's short-term trend back up.
A close below the 1-month lows, QQQ 608.45 or SPY 689.81, would mean the decline is continuing and would reinforce standing aside. A VIX move into the 30+ 'high' band would point the same way.
payload.what_changed: The fear reading now uses the Nov 25 VIX close of 28.29, which replaces the Nov 24 reading used in the previous note. Prices, breadth (8%) and all the gate levels are the same as in the previous note, and DATA reports no new news. The decision stays at stand aside.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
